rewrites.summary:
Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): central Anatolia. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey. What a trans visitor faces here is set by the national framework, and the record documents no province-specific law, ordinance or incident for Kırşehir.

Legal protections and enforcement: there is no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity, and same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition — no marriage, union or adoption — so partner-travel status rests on nothing. A leaked draft omnibus justice package (October 2025) would criminalise conduct and its promotion deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' with up to three years in prison, would restrict gender-affirming healthcare to people aged 25 and over under mandatory infertility and repeated-evaluation conditions, and would expose medical professionals and the trans people they treat to criminal charges, forcing treatment underground.

Practical safety: Pride events have been banned in most years since 2015, with police using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions; the 2025 monitoring report describes hostility turned into explicit state policy, and national monitoring logged an identity-check round-up of about twenty trans women.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Policy turbulence of the parent state: the October 2025 package is a leaked draft, not enacted law, and a rights-monitoring organisation called it one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades. The 2025 monitoring report's counts — six right-to-life violations, three recorded as hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture or ill-treatment violations (up from 51) and 313 liberty violations (about 2.5 times the previous year, mostly detentions) — are country-wide figures with no provincial breakdown, assembled from media and civil-society reports because no official hate-crime statistics exist.

One LGBTI rights organisation was closed, platforms and broadcasters were penalised or withdrew coverage, and artistic events were cancelled.
rewrites.localsOnly: No province-specific resident data is recorded: no cultural-role, birth-register or resident-discrimination fact appears in the sources. The country-wide monitoring counts above are national figures, not provincial resident statistics, and the monitoring report notes that no official hate-crime statistics exist for residents — cases rely on media coverage.

blindSourceSummaries: A rights organisation's news release (29 October 2025) on a leaked draft omnibus package: an amendment would make acting 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' - or promoting it - an offence carrying up to three years in prison; gender-affirming healthcare would be restricted to people aged 25 and over under onerous eligibility rules; and criminal charges could be brought against trans people and the professionals who treat them. The draft was called one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades and withdrawal was urged. No state/province-specific provision appears; the claim is that this national framework is what a visitor stands under.

An association's 2025 human-rights report, titled 'the year of the family: a major siege against LGBTI+ people': hostility toward LGBTI+ people became explicit state/province policy - targeting rhetoric from the head of the parent nation and senior officials, a new family ministry named the implementing ministry, one LGBTI+ rights organisation closed, platforms and broadcasters penalised or withdrawing, artistic events cancelled; it documents six right-to-life violations including three hate-motivated killings (trans people most affected), 89 torture or ill-treatment violations and 313 liberty violations, about 2.5 times the previous year, mostly detentions; no official hate-crime statistics exist and cases rely on media coverage.

A news item (July 2025) on about twenty trans women held for identity checks - names recorded, videos filmed, no official reason given - was not retrievable at fetch time, so its details rest on a research dossier note.

A national-framework reference that governs this record: homosexuality has not been a criminal offence since a historic penal code (1858); transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988; there is no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination; same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition; openly LGBTI people are barred from military service; and Pride events have been banned in most years since 2015 with tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions. A 2026 rights ranking placed the parent nation 47th of 49 assessed. It contains no state/province-specific content.

rewrites.summary:
Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): south-east; conservative. Sources are national-level; no provincial deviation documented. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.

A trans visitor in Muş stands under the national framework: there is no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity, and same-sex marriage is not recognised, so partner-travel or marriage status rests on nothing. A leaked draft judicial-reform package (October 2025) was described as paving the way for criminal charges against LGBT people.

Practical safety: since 2015 local authorities have repeatedly banned and forcibly dispersed Pride marches, with police using water cannon and tear gas against participants; in June 2025 blanket bans were issued against pride marches, police subjected peaceful protesters to unlawful force, over 90 people were arbitrarily detained, and prosecutions of 92 people for participating in pride marches continued at year's end.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Policy turbulence of the parent state: the October 2025 package is a leaked draft, not enacted law, and was described as one of the most alarming rights rollbacks in decades. A country report records three draft law packages targeting LGBTI people made public during 2025 — an unprecedented assault that would criminalise expression of LGBTI identities and consensual same-sex relations and make legal gender recognition nearly impossible — but they were ultimately not submitted to parliament. The report's findings are country-wide, and no provincial breakdown for this province appears.
rewrites.localsOnly: Resident-facing facts from the national framework: transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988; openly LGBTI people are barred from serving in the military, and conscripts who declare their homosexuality are classed under a definition of homosexuality as a 'psychosexual illness', must provide photographic proof, and risk their unfit report leaking publicly. No provincial resident data is recorded.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The record is a model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta) and is not independently verifiable here, and no provincial series exists to check against. Enactment of the October 2025 draft is unresolved, and the three 2025 draft packages were not submitted to parliament. Early-2026 press reports of legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex' were not included in the year's judicial reform package. No source addresses identity-document or border-screening practice for trans visitors, and no partner-travel or marriage information beyond the non-recognition facts is recorded.

Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): conservative interior. Sources are national-level; no provincial deviation documented. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.

A trans visitor in Niğde stands under the national framework: there is no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity, and same-sex marriage, civil unions, domestic partnerships and joint adoption are not recognised, so partner-travel or marriage status rests on nothing. A leaked draft judicial-reform package (October 2025) was described as paving the way for criminal charges against LGBT people, one of the most alarming rights rollbacks in decades.

Practical safety: Pride events have been banned in most years since 2015, with police using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against participants; in June 2025 blanket bans were issued against pride marches, police subjected peaceful protesters to unlawful force, over 90 people were arbitrarily detained, and prosecutions of 92 people for participating in pride marches continued at year's end.
rewrites.tangentialFactors: Policy turbulence of the parent state: the October 2025 package is a leaked draft, not enacted law. A country report records three draft law packages targeting LGBTI people made public during 2025 — an unprecedented assault that would criminalise expression of LGBTI identities and consensual same-sex relations and make legal gender recognition nearly impossible — but they were ultimately not submitted to parliament. Litigation flux: a court case to close an LGBTI association was overruled by the top court, a court ordered an association dissolved in December 2025 over 'obscene' images, and a February 2026 press report of legislation criminalising public advocacy of 'behaviour contrary to biological sex' was not included in the year's judicial reform package, whose passage removed provisions discriminating against LGBTI people and made symbolic same-sex weddings possible. A 2026 rights ranking placed the parent nation 47th of 49 assessed.
rewrites.localsOnly: Resident-facing facts from the national framework: transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988; openly LGBTI people are barred from serving in the military — the armed forces' health regulation defines homosexuality as a 'psychosexual illness', conscripts who declare it must provide photographic proof, and those receiving an unfit report may face later discrimination in public life. No provincial resident data is recorded.
rewrites.outOfScopeNotes: The record is a model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta) and is not independently verifiable here; no provincial series exists to check against. Enactment of the October 2025 draft is unresolved, and the 2025 draft packages were not submitted to parliament. No source addresses identity-document or border-screening practice for trans visitors, and no partner-travel or marriage information beyond the non-recognition facts is recorded.
